messages:
incident-bot: [P1] runtime-alert: continuous-batching timeouts + KV cache memory spike detected for model rwd-llama-13b in us-west-2. p99 latency > 10s, eviction rate rising rapidly, ~40-60% 5xx across a subset of hosts. Auto-escalation to on-call.

maya: on it. seeing continuous-batching workers with huge batch token windows and KV cache mem climb to 94%. likely misconfig + workload shift.

trent: i'm oncall. handoff: i have the lead. ETA 2m to triage. which customers hit?

deploy-bot: rolling alert: config-change-detector flagged recent config push to continuous_batching.* at 10:12PT. diff id: cfg-2026-03-15-1256.

maya: confirmed — a config rollout this morning increased max_batch_tokens=8192 and max_num_seqs=256 in us-west-2 (intended for other clusters). looks like selector mis-scoped.

sara: support -> customer-impact: enterprise customers reporting 5xx: AcmeCorp, NovaHealth, BrightPlan. estimated affected requests ~1.3M in last 15m. CS already opened tickets.

devon: graphs: KV hit rate dropped, eviction calls skyrocketed, GC thrash on GPU host side. continuous-batching queues piling up, timeouts because we're exceeding memory and hitting eviction thrash.

trent: mitigation plan (short-term): 1) revert mis-scoped config selector immediately in us-west-2 2) reduce continuous batching params to safe defaults (max_batch_tokens=1024, max_num_seqs=16) 3) enable stateless fallback route for critical customers 4) monitor.

maya: agree. do canary first (3 hosts) then region-wide. i'll run the config patch.

maya: command i'll run now:
```bash
# canary patch: runtime config (us-west-2 canary pool)
redwoodctl runtime set-config --cluster us-west-2 --pool canary --param continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens=1024 \
  --param continuous_batching.max_num_seqs=16 --reason "emergency revert - mis-scoped rollout"
```

deploy-bot: started rollout: cfg-rollback-3860001234. canary 3 hosts -> in progress. UI: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/cfg-rollback-3860001234

trent: i'm patching the routing flag for critical customers to fallback stateless route:
```bash
redwoodctl routes update --region us-west-2 --customer AcmeCorp, NovaHealth,BrightPlan --set route=stateless_fallback --ttl 900
```

maya: after canary patches we should also reduce the eviction aggressiveness threshold to avoid thrash: set kvcache.eviction.pause_ms=200 to give GC breathing room.

maya: command:
```bash
# dynamic config patch
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens":"1024","continuous_batching.max_num_seqs":"16","kvcache.eviction.pause_ms":"200"}}'
```

trent: canary results: within 90s p99 dropped from ~11s -> 450ms on canaries, eviction rate down 70%. promoting to region.

deploy-bot: rollout to region us-west-2 started. phased: 25% -> 50% -> 100%. estimated completion 8m.

maya: alerting note: observed persistent long-lived KV entries from earlier high max_batch_tokens. we'll need a background truncation job to remove oversized entries over the next hour. scheduling now.

ashley: assigned to run truncation job and validate KV store consistency. I'll post results.

trent: customer impact update: CS reported reduced errors after canary; AcmeCorp sees recovery; NovaHealth still seeing intermittent 502s for a small percent of requests (~0.8%).

sara: messaging ready: "We experienced an elevated error rate and latency in us-west-2 between 10:12PT and 10:30PT due to a mis-scoped continuous batching config rollout. The team has reverted the config and most services are recovered — CS will follow up with impacted customers."

devon: root cause notes for postmortem: config rollout included cluster selector bug that applied high batching limits to us-west-2. Combined with a workload spike of longer sequences the KV cache grew beyond expected working set causing eviction GC thrash and batch timeouts.

trent: action items (short):
- audit recent config rollouts and add stricter selector validation (maya)
- add automatic canary gating when continuous_batching params change (devon)
- add emergency circuit to disable continuous batching if eviction > 80% for 2m (trent)
- customer followups and incidents page update (sara)

maya: i'm adding a safety guard in the config service to reject >4096 max_batch_tokens without explicit override + two-person approve for region-wide changes.

ashley: truncation job started at 10:24PT. initial pass reclaimed ~18% KV mem. observing gradual stabilization.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: config applied to 100% us-west-2 at 10:30PT. No failures in rollout.

trent: monitoring: p99 stabilized ~380-520ms across the region, eviction calls back to baseline. moving incident to mitigation -> monitoring.

incident-bot: Status update: P1 -> P2 at 10:37PT (mitigation achieved).

sara: CS update posted to customer tickets and status page draft ready. will mark "resolved" once we confirm 30m of stable telemetry.

maya: locking the config that caused issue and filing a postmortem draft.

trent: handing back oncall to maya (end of shift for me). leaving triage notes in the incident thread.

maya: thanks. I'll continue monitoring for 30m then begin postmortem writeup.

sara: final customer-impact summary for postmortem: ~1.3M affected requests, peak error rate 52% in targeted host pool, full recovery within ~18 minutes after rollback, 3 enterprise customers directly reported incidents.

devon: logging snippet captured earlier for root cause:
```
[2026-03-15T10:18:22Z] batcher: queued batch size 8192 tokens, num_seqs=240, kvcache.alloc 95% -> eviction triggered -> timeout=12000ms -> client error 504
```

trent: tagging this thread with incident:kv-cache-cont-batch-misconfig for PM/ops follow-up.

maya: locking. good work team. closing realtime mitigation. next: full RCA and release checklist update.
